page: Microsoft Azure D32a_v4 is a general-purpose virtual machine belonging to the DAv4 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It is equipped with an AMD EPYC 7452 processor utilizing the x86_64 architecture. The configuration provides 32 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 16 physical cores with 2 threads per core, operating at a clock speed of 3.35 GHz. The CPU features 32 KB of L1d cache, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache, with support for AVX, AES, SHA_NI, and FMA instructions.

The server is provisioned with 128.0 GB of system memory, yielding a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. It includes 819 GB of local storage, providing built-in space for temporary data and caching. There are no GPUs or complimentary public IPv4 addresses bundled with this instance type.

Performance benchmarks position the D32a_v4 as a capable mid-tier system. It achieves top-tier status in the PassMark memory score and strong results in stress-ng single-core CPU performance. Multi-core CPU performance, memory bandwidth, and database operations fall within the average range. For language model workloads, it exhibits strong text generation speeds with small 135M models, but performance drops to the bottom 25% for prompt processing on large 70B models.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the D32a_v4 offers a balanced resource density suitable for mainstream enterprise workloads. The combination of 32 dedicated vCPUs, 128 GB of RAM, and local storage makes it well-suited for general-purpose applications, relational databases, web serving, and software compilation, though it is less optimal for large-scale LLM inference.
